title: Microsoft Copilot for Finance: What It Is and How It Compares
summary: Microsoft Copilot for Finance is an AI assistant for finance inside Excel, Outlook, and Teams. What it does, how it works, what it costs, and how it compares.
body_markdown:
Microsoft has brought AI into the finance function the way it brings most things: inside the apps finance teams already live in. **Microsoft Copilot for Finance** is an AI assistant that sits in Excel, Outlook, and Teams and helps with specific finance tasks, connected to the data in your ERP. For teams already standardized on Microsoft 365 and Dynamics, it is an easy on-ramp to AI. This guide explains what it is, what it actually does, what it costs, and where it fits versus a purpose-built finance agent platform.


## **What is Microsoft Copilot for Finance?**


Microsoft Copilot for Finance, now branded "Finance in Microsoft 365 Copilot," is a role-based extension of Microsoft 365 Copilot that adds AI assistance for finance professionals directly inside the Microsoft apps they use every day. It[launched in public preview in February 2024](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/blog/2024/02/29/introducing-microsoft-copilot-for-finance-transform-finance-with-next-generation-ai-in-microsoft-365/) and reached[general availability on October 20, 2025](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics-365/blog/it-professional/2025/10/20/empowering-finance-with-an-ai-assistant-in-microsoft-365-copilot/) , with its financial reconciliation capability GA and several others still in preview.


> Copilot for Finance is not a new application you log into. It is AI dropped into the tools finance already uses, Excel, Outlook, Teams, so a person can do certain tasks faster without leaving them.


## **What Microsoft Copilot for Finance does**


Its capabilities are specific finance tasks inside Microsoft 365 apps:


- **Financial reconciliation (in Excel).** Reconciles two data sets, lets the AI determine matching rules, flags unmatched transactions, suggests matches, and generates a reconciliation report. This is the generally available capability, and it can run in an autonomous mode on a schedule or trigger.
- **Variance analysis (in Excel).** Works on pivot tables of time-series data to identify variances and outliers and explain the drivers, via natural-language criteria. (Preview.)
- **Customer communications and collections (in Outlook).** Pulls ERP invoice and payment data, drafts context-aware replies, suggests priority accounts, and saves summaries back to the ERP. (Preview.)
- **Data preparation (in Excel).** Cleans and reshapes exported ERP data for analysis. (Preview.)


## **How it works and what it connects to**


Copilot for Finance runs inside Excel, Outlook, and Teams and connects those apps to your system of record, so users can complete tasks without signing into the ERP. It[integrates natively with Dynamics 365 Finance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/release-plan/2024wave1/finance-supply-chain/microsoft-copilot-finance/) and also connects to Dynamics 365 Business Central and SAP, with custom connectors to other ERPs buildable through Microsoft Copilot Studio. The richest, most native integration is with Dynamics 365.


## **What it costs**


Copilot for Finance requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. At general availability it is offered at no additional cost to Microsoft 365 Copilot customers, installed by IT from Microsoft AppSource. In practice it also requires a connected ERP (Dynamics 365, Business Central, SAP, or a custom connector) to be useful. So the real cost is your Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing plus the ERP it connects to, rather than a separate finance-software line.


## **Is it an assistant or an agent?**


This is the key question for anyone evaluating it. Copilot for Finance is primarily an **assistant** : it helps a person complete a task and keeps a human in the loop. You review and confirm reconciliation matches; you review and send the collections emails it drafts. The one exception is the financial reconciliation agent, which has an autonomous mode that can run reconciliations on a schedule or trigger and notify you when done.


> Copilot for Finance mostly helps you do the work, with one task, reconciliation, that it can run on its own. That is a meaningful distinction from an agent platform designed to run whole finance workflows end to end across your systems.


## **Microsoft Copilot for Finance vs. a finance agent platform**


Copilot for Finance and a dedicated finance agent platform like[Concourse](https://www.concourse.ai/) solve overlapping problems in different ways:


Copilot for Finance Finance agent platform


Model Assistant inside Microsoft apps Agents that run workflows end to end


Scope Specific tasks (recon, variance, collections) The close, forecasting, AR/AP, reporting


Ecosystem Microsoft 365 + Dynamics (native) Any stack, 100+ systems


Autonomy Mostly assistive; recon can run autonomously Agents execute, human approves at the gates


Requirement Microsoft 365 Copilot license + ERP Connects to your existing stack


The honest summary: if your team lives entirely in Microsoft 365 and Dynamics and wants AI help inside Excel and Outlook, Copilot for Finance is a natural fit. If you want AI agents to actually run finance workflows, reconciliations, the close, forecasting, collections, and reporting, across whatever systems you already use, with every output traceable to source, that is a different category. See how that works in[agentic finance](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/agentic-finance) and the[best AI tools for finance teams](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/best-ai-tools-for-finance-teams) .


## **Frequently asked questions**


### **What is Microsoft Copilot for Finance?**


It is an AI assistant for finance professionals that works inside Microsoft 365 apps (Excel, Outlook, Teams), connected to the ERP, to help with tasks like reconciliation, variance analysis, and collections communications. It is now branded "Finance in Microsoft 365 Copilot" and reached general availability in October 2025.


### **What does Microsoft Copilot for Finance do?**


Financial reconciliation and data preparation in Excel, variance analysis on pivot tables, and customer communications and collections in Outlook, all drawing on ERP data. Reconciliation is generally available (and can run autonomously); the others are in preview.


### **How much does Microsoft Copilot for Finance cost?**


It requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and, at general availability, is offered at no additional cost to those customers. It also needs a connected ERP (Dynamics 365, Business Central, SAP, or a custom connector) to be useful, so the real cost is your Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing plus your ERP.


### **Is Microsoft Copilot for Finance an AI agent?**


Mostly it is an assistant that helps a human complete tasks within Microsoft apps, with a human reviewing and confirming. The financial reconciliation capability is the exception, with an autonomous mode. It is not a platform built to run full finance workflows end to end across your stack.


## **The bottom line**


Microsoft Copilot for Finance brings AI into the finance function through the Microsoft apps teams already use, helping with reconciliation, variance analysis, and collections, and letting reconciliation run autonomously. For organizations all-in on Microsoft 365 and Dynamics, it is a convenient way to add AI assistance. Its boundaries are the Microsoft ecosystem and a task-by-task assistive model, rather than agents that own entire finance workflows across any stack.
